Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase! The two umpires make their way out to the middle followed by Sri Lankan players who are spreading out to take the field. Indian opening pair of Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill stride out to the centre. Asitha Fernando is handed the new ball and is on top of his mark, raring to go. Let's play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

With a target of 231 runs set for India, Sri Lanka will carry some momentum into the next innings, knowing they can restrict the Indian side if they make full use of the assistance available on the pitch especially with their three spinners. While India would have been satisfied with this target at the start of the game, they will need to play sensibly to achieve it. The game is nicely poised at the halfway mark. Will Sri Lanka start with spin right away and make an early impact? Or will India, with their batting firepower, cruise through the chase? Stick around as we find out with the chase unfolding in a bit.

Dunith Wellalage, the star of the first innings is down for a chat.  Wellalage says that he had prepared for this wicket and tried to play his natural game. Adds that he looked to rotate the strike. He backs Wanindu Hasaranga and the Sri Lankan pacers to defend this total. Feels that it is not easy to bat and need to bowl in partnerships to put the pressure.

However, towards the end, Dunith Wellalage put on a fine display, scoring his maiden ODI fifty and staying unbeaten at 67 runs putting up a 46 runs partnership along with Akila Dananjaya helping his side cross the 220-run mark, which had seemed far-fetched at one point.

Janith Liyanage and Dunith Wellalage then absorbed the pressure, enduring a few probing overs from Kuldeep and Sundar. They counter-attacked when Shubman Gill was brought in for an over, taking 14 runs off him and easing the pressure. A crucial moment came when Janith Liyanage walked off after a huge appeal for a caught at slip, only to see on replays that he had not made contact with the ball. Their 41-run partnership was vital for Sri Lanka, considering how the game had unfolded thus far.

The Indian spinners maintained the pressure, with Axar Patel removing the dangerous Sadeera Samarawickrama cheaply. Despite wickets tumbling around him, Pathum Nissanka carried his form from the T20Is and kept one end strong ensuring he notched up a well-deserved half-century, making the most of a dropped catch by Mohammed Siraj at 21. Washington Sundar and Kuldeep Yadav kept things tight and created enough doubts in the batters' minds, taking two more wickets, including that of Nissanka.

Mohammed Siraj and Arshdeep Singh began the attack with tight lines and lengths, preventing the home side from gaining early momentum. Avishka Fernando struggled and was dismissed by Siraj in the third over for just one run, putting Sri Lanka on the back foot from the outset. Kusal Mendis managed a start but never looked settled, falling to Shivam Dube after the first Powerplay.
A strong comeback by Sri Lanka to post 230 runs on the board by the end of the first innings all thanks to some exceptional batting from Dunith Wellalage.

A single to end the innings! Arshdeep Singh slips in a slower bouncer, over middle, Dunith Wellalage backs away and tries to slap it up and over backward point. Gets a feather on it and it goes on the bounce to the keeper, KL Rahul which allows the batters to scamper across for a quick run. 8 runs off the final over and Sri Lanka end with 230 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the national anthems. A sparse crowd is in on a Friday afternoon in Colombo, but it should build as the day progresses. The Indian players are in a huddle near the ropes before taking their respective positions on the field. The two umpires are followed by the two Sri Lankan openers, Avishka Fernando and Pathum Nissanka. It will be Mohammed Siraj to kickstart the proceedings with the new ball for India. Two slips in place. Away we go...

We are moments away from the first ball in this series opener, but before that, Charith Asalanka and Rohit Sharma will lead their respective sides out for the national anthems. The Indian players and support staff are wearing black armbands in memory of the former Indian batter and coach, Anshuman Gaekwad, who passed away earlier this week. It will be the Indian national anthem first, followed by that of Sri Lanka.

Shreyas Iyer is in for a chat. He says that he looks to bring out his natural game, not think much about the conditions and bat freely. Tells that with the kind of team they have, they will want to just go out and execute their plans well. Concludes that he has worked with Gautam Gambhir in the past and appreciates him for the kind of freedom and confidence he gives to a player. Further says that he brings out the best in the players and you get to learn a lot from him.
India (Playing XI) - Rohit Sharma (C), Shubman Gill, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer, KL Rahul (WK), Washington Sundar, Shivam Dube, Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Mohammed Siraj.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Avishka Fernando, Kusal Mendis (WK), Sadeera Samarawickrama, Charith Asalanka (C), Janith Liyanage, Wanindu Hasaranga, Dunith Wellalage, Akila Dananjaya, Asitha Fernando, Mohamed Shiraz (On ODI debut).

The captain of India, Rohit Sharma says that they are okay with bowling first. Tells that the pitch tends to get slower as the game progresses. Further says that they have played a lot of cricket here and know the conditions at this venue. Feels that this series is a good opportunity to know where they stand. Informs that Virat Kohli, KL Rahul, Shreyas Iyer and Kuldeep Yadav return to the side. Also informs that Shivam Dube will feature in this game. Reckons that they have a pretty decent balance. Says that despite not crossing the finishing line at the ODI World Cup, there were a lot of positives for them. Adds that it is important to create an atmosphere where the players can express themselves.

Charith Asalanka, the skipper of Sri Lanka says they will bat first because it looks pretty dry. Adds that Mohamed Shiraz makes his debut and they are going with 6 batters and 5 bowlers. Says that they have to improve their mental skills, especially after the last game but they will look to play well and focus on the present. Concludes that injuries are a concern for a captain but they will need to face these situations and do well going ahead with the second lineup.
TOSS - Sri Lanka have won the flip of the coin and they have opted to BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Scott Styris is near the deck. He starts by telling the dimensions of the square boundaries - 77 metres to one side and 73 meters to the other. Feels that there are plenty of runs to be had on this surface. Informs that this wicket was used for Qualifier 2 in the Lanka Premier League. Adds that despite its use in the recent past, the surface does not have much wear and tear. States that the wicket has very little grass covering and feels that it may turn a little bit and could be a bit tacky. Opines that it will not be anything like what we saw in the 3rd T20I. Reckons that the ball will slide nicely onto the bat under lights.

India certainly look like a dominant force against a side facing significant challenges, but Sri Lanka will believe they have what it takes to put forth a strong game and beat any team on the given day. Can India continue their successful run in the island nation, or will the home team stage a turbulent fightback to win this first game? We shall soon find out as the toss and team updates come to you in a bit.

On the other hand, India have pushed the reset button, with Rohit Sharma and Gautam Gambhir seemingly crafting meticulous plans ahead of the next big event, the Champions Trophy. The team is further bolstered by the return of KL Rahul and Shreyas Iyer, who will be eager to pick up where they left off last year. Kuldeep Yadav could prove to be a crucial asset, and it is very likely that this team may also see a couple of debutants making their mark in ODIs.

After suffering a 3-0 defeat in the T20I series, Sri Lanka face additional challenges with injuries to key pacers Matheesha Pathirana and Dilshan Madushanka, complicating matters even further for skipper Charith Asalanka. The fast-bowling department is in disarray, with Asitha Fernando remaining as the sole frontline seamer. He may be paired with either of the new replacements, Mohamed Shiraz or Eshan Malinga. However, with the pitch favouring spin, Sri Lanka's quality spinners can help compensate for the inexperience in the pace unit. The inconsistency in the middle order has been a significant concern over the years, which the team will look to address quickly to ease some pressure on the top order.

Hello and a warm welcome to the opening match of the eagerly anticipated three-game ODI series between India and Sri Lanka, set to begin at the iconic R. Premadasa Stadium in Colombo. Excitement is building up as fans worldwide await Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma's return to the field. Sri Lanka face a significant challenge, especially with injury concerns, as they aim to avenge their recent whitewash in the T20I series.
